h: The Well of Torah and the Shepherd of Yisrael

p: At all the meals of Shabbos
"A psalm of David: Hashem is my shepherd, etc."
and at the third meal in the middle of the meal,
In the holy Zohar on this parashah (183b),
the alef is the whole of all,
for the alef rests in completeness.
and the letter hei the middah of Malchus,
and the letter vav, which is a "true letter,"
the aspect of the Name Havayah;
and it is the sum of the three holinesses of Shabbos,
who hold on to the supernal whole of all;
and the alef, which includes all."
כּוֹלֵל גַּם כֵּן ג׳ קְדוּשּׁוֹת הַנִּזְכָּר
also includes the three holinesses mentioned,
And it is written after it,
"His people and the flock of His pasture":
and Yisrael is called the flock of His pasture;
and as it says, "Hashem is my shepherd, etc.,
He leads me beside still waters"
is the aspect of the Oral Torah,
for the Written Torah is likened to bread,
and drink of the wine I have mixed":
the bread of the Written Torah,
and the wine of the Oral Torah
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא עֵקֶב רעא, ב)
and the Oral Torah is likened
like the well, which had in it
the taste of all kinds of beverages
like the mann, which had in it
And this is what it says,
"And from there to Be'erah; that is the well":
for in truth it is all one,
is included in the Written Torah,
is the aspect of the moon,
And so it is expounded in the Gemara (Kiddushin 30b):
What is "with enemies in the gate"?
and they do not move from there
עַד שֶׁנַּעֲשִׂים אוֹהֲבִים זֶה אֶת זֶה
until they become friends of one another,
and Rashi explains, thus it is expounded:
a war that is through the book;
there is love at its end.
And one also needs to understand,
what is the wording of the pasuk,
in the book of the wars of Hashem":
to the matter of the streams of Arnon?
But it follows what was said,
is likened to beverages and to water;
וְנָהָר צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת לוֹ ב׳ צְדָדִים
and a river must have two banks
that are higher than the water,
with the water in the middle;
and so too in the Oral Torah
there is a right and a left,
and forty-nine ways to declare impure;
and from this comes the dispute,
the war that is through the book,
And regarding the crossings of the streams of Arnon,
it is brought in the Gemara (Berachos 54b):
the mountains clung to one another
וּבְמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (בַּמִּדְבַּר רַבָּה יט, כה) אִיתָא
And in the Midrash Rabbah (Bamidbar Rabbah 19:25) it is brought
that the mountain of Eretz Yisrael trembled,
because it was of Eretz Yisrael,
a parable of a maidservant, etc.;
that the two mountains became level,
that in truth, after the dispute,
then there is love at its end,
for there is no dispute at all;
"They were all given by one Shepherd;
And this is what it says after the miracle
of the crossings of the streams of Arnon,
in the book of the wars of Hashem":
that is, a war that is through the book,
that is, that afterward there is love at its end,
as they said in the Gemara.
"And from there to Be'erah; that is the well":
and as it says in the holy Zohar:
the whole of male and female,
וְכֵן כְּתִיב אַחַר כָּךְ (שָׁם כא, יח)
And so it is written afterward (Bamidbar 21:18),
"which the nobles of the people dug,
with the lawgiver, with their staffs":
"with the lawgiver" — this is Moshe Rabbeinu,
"for there the portion of the lawgiver is hidden";
that is, the entire Oral Torah
is from the Written Torah of Moshe.
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמַר בַּגְּמָרָא (שָׁם יד, א)
along the lines of what the Gemara says (Chagigah 14a)
on "the staff of bread and the staff of water":
masters of Talmud and masters of Aggadah;
שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד יֵשׁ לוֹ מִשְׁעָן שֶׁלּוֹ
for each one has his own staff.
אִם מֵשִׂים אָדָם עַצְמוֹ כַּמִּדְבָּר וְכוּלֵּי
if a person makes himself like a wilderness, etc.,
the Torah is given to him as a gift, etc.;
and if he becomes haughty, etc.
וְהוּא מוּסָב עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
And this refers to the Oral Torah,
which leave a high place, etc.,
in the lowliest of vessels, etc.,
as they said in the Gemara (Taanis 7a).
And on Shabbos, since the three meals
therefore we say at all the meals
the psalm "Hashem is my shepherd, etc.":
he has nothing at all from his own effort,
which is the aspect of the Oral Torah,
And at the first two meals we say,
who said, "The God Who shepherds me, etc.,"
which is the trait of lowliness and humility,
and he said, "From where will my help come?"
לָכֵן אוֹמְרִים מִזְמוֹר זֶה ה׳ רוֹעִי
therefore we say this psalm, "Hashem is my shepherd,"
in the middle of the meal and after eating.
